newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish zloty eyes higher ground after idle session.
newsitem.headline: Polish zloty eyes higher ground after idle session.

text.p: The Polish zloty held basically idle against the basket of currencies on Thursday but dealers said the local currency may test higher ground on Friday.

They said the zloty, which tracked dollar/mark moves throughout today's session without much direction, may build up steam on Friday on investment and foreigner purchases of Polish treasuries and climb to resistance at 2.5 percent from parity.

"The zloty was stable around 2.35 percent from the parity rate today, but interest in Polish paper should again push the zloty up towards 2.5 percent in the near-term," said Pawel Dudzinski, forex dealer at Pekao SA.
The zloty closed at 2.38/2.31 percent from the trading band centre, virtually flat from Wednesday's 2.40/2.33 close.
It finished at 3.0010/30 to the dollar, up from 2.30020/40 on Wednesday and at 1.8300/15 to the mark, down from 1.8290/10.

However, dealers said that if foreign purchases of treasuries materialise and push the zloty towards 2.5 percent, the central bank would likely again step in with a currency buying intervention to knock the local currency down.
"It seems the central bank doesn't mind if the zloty trades in a band between 2.0-2.5 percent from parity, but it is likely to guard the upside carefully," one foreign bank dealer said.
Overnight deposit rates closed nearly three points down after volatile trade on the last day of January's required reserve period, dealers said.

O/N rates, which closed at 17.20/19.00 percent versus Wednesday's 21.60/21.80, tumbled to lows around 12 percent this morning before a NBP-bill sale payable on Thursday pulled up rates in the early afternoon.
Tomorrow/next rates closed unchanged at 21.60/80 percent, signaling that one-day rates would on Friday again straddle the central bank's main drainage rate of 21.64 percent for 14-days.
